description: Arcep publishes monthly statistics of IPv6 use for internet access, the share of users connected in IPv6 by their provider, as part of its barometer of the transition to IPv6 in France. Since September 2025 the values are monthly averages combining four measurement sources, Google, Akamai, Facebook and APNIC, with three sources out of four deemed enough; the data give values for French providers and for the 100 countries with most internet users, with a rank over all countries. Coverage: France by provider and countries worldwide, monthly from October 2013. Format and access: CSV, JSON and GeoJSON files on data.gouv.fr; free under the Licence Ouverte 2.0 (Etalab). Caveats: the methodology and country codes changed in September 2025, so older downloads differ; the measures reflect content-side observations, not network inventories. Simulation uses: a technology adoption indicator for internet routing infrastructure and planning of address-space transition. Related records: the NRO and RIR statistics give address allocations, and RIPE Atlas and CAIDA give routing measurements.
